text: Using gpt2-small as the weak supervisor and qwen2.5-3b as the strong student, we evaluated adaptive label smoothing weighted by per-sample loss drop, with smoothing_max set to 0.3, across num_seeds = 10 seeds. The weak supervisor reached 0.56 accuracy and the strong model's ceiling was 0.74, while the strongly-supervised-equivalent transfer accuracy under weak labels was 0.73 with a standard error of 0.01. The resulting performance gap recovered (PGR) was 0.93 with a standard error of 0.05, compared with a baseline PGR of 0.23. The margin between the method's PGR and the baseline is substantially larger than two standard errors of the PGR estimate, so the recovery under this method exceeds the baseline by more than sampling noise would explain. Caveats: the baseline PGR is reported without an accompanying standard error, so the comparison rests on the method's uncertainty alone, and results come from a single weak–strong model pair and one smoothing_max setting, leaving generality untested.
